Treat princess as a broad adult royal archetype, not a single Joseon-only costume: choose one coherent register such as Korean court, Chinese hanfu court, Western ballroom royalty, modern royal heiress, incognito heir, or fallen/exiled royal.

Royal identity must read through visible regalia, inherited-rank posture, lineage object, crest, attendants, throne/court space, official public-display context, or palace-security context, not just a pretty dress.
Do not collapse every princess prompt into hanbok/Joseon palace; do not turn it into generic cosplay, pin-up monarchy, minors-coding, or disconnected fantasy costume.
femme fatale reinterpreted as a powerful, intelligent, dangerous woman who controls the gaze and the situation: the symbol of potential ruin, not a sexy villainess stereotype
she is the subject who watches and decides; the camera or viewer is the one being observed and unsettled through gaze reversal

keep the role outfit readable; the femme fatale layer changes power, posture, gaze direction, light, and symbolic props rather than turning the image into lingerie, cleavage-centric framing, or a pin-up
express danger through noir and symbolist grammar: chiaroscuro, deep shadow, reflection or doubling, threshold framing, wilted-flower or poison omen, and withheld intent

make intelligence and leverage visible in the frame: at least one information-control anchor such as a sealed file, guest book, ledger, calling card, phone message, key, decree, or withheld result should sit near her face, hand, table edge, or foreground, not only in the mood

danger may also be expressed as magnetic, deliberate allure where being drawn in is itself the trap: a honey-trap or spider-and-web register in which she chooses the encounter, sets the lure, and reads the mark; this is still agency, intelligence, and control, never passive availability or submission

agency over availability: no come-hither pose, no bedroom-eyes expression, no parted-lips invitation, no submissive posture, no nudity, no explicit or fetish content, and no depicted violence, blood, victim, or injury

frame her through face, eyes, hands, and symbolic evidence in an upper-body, head-and-shoulders, waist-up, or detail crop; if a low-angle camera is used, frame it as dominance through face, eyes, posture, and stance from a respectful distance, never as an objectifying full-body or pin-up body angle
the princess styling reads as political power and lethal intelligence in a poisoned court, not decorative beauty
the phoenix hairpin catches a quiet omen-like glint, with an unsigned decree or sealed court order nearby as the information she may reveal or destroy; she is the one who decides fates in this court
broad adult princess or royal-heir portrait with a coherent cultural or era register
royal lineage, public display, succession, ceremony, modern nobility, incognito identity, or exile facets
visible regalia, crown or tiara, court ornament, lineage object, palace, ballroom, court, or modern royal setting
femme fatale as power, intelligence, danger, and the symbol of ruin, never simple seduction
gaze reversal where the viewer becomes the observed object
noir and symbolist grammar: chiaroscuro, reflection-doubling, threshold, wilted omen, poison omen, withheld intent
intellectual danger and leverage made visible through information-control anchors near the face, hands, table edge, or foreground
two legitimate registers: cold information-control authority, and magnetic lure-as-weapon where the invitation itself is the trap
role outfit preserved while femme fatale identity appears through power, gaze, light, posture, and symbolic props
